reason: The Assembly adopted the law on 27 June 2025 and the regulator reports that it applies from 1 January 2026. No item shows the by-laws, entity lists or new response teams in place, so application date is not treated as implementation. The Commission finds sufficient but not full alignment with the EU cybersecurity acquis.

The law was still a plan at this date: the Commission asked for its adoption and the Reform Agenda set June 2025. The ITU profile of February 2022 listed it as an existing enabler, but the Commission's 2022 report says the draft was not adopted, and the later adoption supports the Commission.

The State Audit Office, an independent source, confirms the portal has been in use since 2019, but finds low use (0.556 services per registered user), and the 2025 strategy reports 314 services and about 13 of 100 adults registered. Use is real but limited. The Commission and the audit differ on access for people with disabilities, which does not change the status.

The State Audit Office found the platform operational but used by only a small share of institutions, and the Commission confirms use by customs and few institutions overall. The 2025 strategy gives 63 connected institutions, of which 37 actively exchange data. I rely on the audit and Commission over the screening statements that it simply functions.

The Commission states that the agreement was fully implemented and that North Macedonia has benefited from the roaming-free zone since 2021, and the regulator collects quarterly operator data on the regime. The regulator dates the start to 1 June 2021 and the Commission to 1 July 2021, which does not change the status.
The agreement was in force and charges were being progressively reduced, but roaming charges were not yet eliminated. Roam like at home followed in July 2021, which is the change that matters.

This is a Reform Agenda target to raise e-services by 50% by June 2027, and the Commission still described it as a measure in April 2026. No item reports the target met. The stated 2024 baseline differs between sources (392 and 264), which does not affect the status.

The Council was formally established, but the Commission says it was not active and the State Audit Office finds it met once and calls it non-functioning, while North Macedonia told the 2023 screening it was in place. I give more weight to the audit and say so here; the 2025 cyber strategy proposes merging it into another council. Sources also date its formation differently (2019 and July 2020).

The Commission reported the Council as established and composed of three ministers. This is the status before the 2022 report said it was inactive; the formation date is disputed between 2019 and July 2020.
The Commission gives specific use: the e-market system awarded 258 small value procurements in 2023. The target of 800 awards by December 2026 remains a plan, and no item reports whether it was met.

A working group started in 2021, but the State Audit Office finds in 2025 that no AI strategy has been adopted, and the 2025 ICT strategy still lists drafting one as an activity. The working group is a step towards the strategy and not the strategy itself.

Commission technical checks confirm the system is partially operational in several institutions, and the government reports a pilot in 22 of about 140 central institutions using a small part of its potential. This is partial roll-out, so I do not rate it in practice for the unified system; the target of all central institutions is December 2026.
The unified system was a planned Reform Agenda step with a December 2026 target. The later Commission checks show the move to partial operation.
The State Audit Office records the strategy and action plan as adopted. The measures in these items are stated as aims, and no item shows them carried out as a whole.

The Commission reports the platform upgraded and reaching 312 online services by September 2025. It gives no evidence of use, and it asked as late as 2023 for upgrading to meet the Services Directive, so I do not rate it in practice.
The Commission said preparations continued but remained at an early stage. The 2022 report then describes an available platform, which is the change that matters.

The Government adopted the Roadmap by conclusion, as the State Audit Office records. The 2025 strategy says its principles lack enforcement mechanisms, and no item shows the Roadmap itself carried out. Sources differ on the date (late 2023 and January 2024), which does not change the status.

Alignment remains a stated plan: the 2023 screening and 2025 strategy describe future or ongoing work, and the Commission still asks for it in 2024 and 2025. The State Audit Office found in 2022 no study of alignment behind the ministry's claim to follow EIF 2.0.

The Government ordered the plan carried out in August 2025 and the gap analyses were submitted in December 2025, but the transposing law, decisions and rulebook were still drafts sent to the Commission for review. The evidence is the regulator's own report and stops in March 2026.
The Commission reports that Parliament ratified the Protocol in June 2021. No item shows separate implementing measures attributed to it.
The amendments were adopted on 10 June 2024 and the Commission confirms the new Ministry of Digital Transformation was set up. The items show the institution in place, not how well it works.

The Commission reports that the Bureau launched an updated system on 1 April 2025, following earlier upgrades. It also records limited progress, and no item gives evidence of use of the updated version.
The items are Reform Agenda and project descriptions with a December 2027 target. No item shows the network rolled out.

The 2025 Law on Electronic Communications (INT-MKD-0023) repeals the earlier law, listing Official Gazette 92/21 among its amendments, from the day it starts to apply, 1 June 2026. The successor is therefore in application at the freeze date.

The amendments were adopted in April 2021 and the regulator adopted the implementing by-laws, but North Macedonia itself says not all amendments are fully implemented. No item shows the prior security approval actually used.
The items set out a Reform Agenda reform and describe what should follow. No item reports the expanded use of e-customs services under this reform.

The 2025 law designates the Ministry and the regulator as competent authorities, and the cyber strategy names the Ministry. No item shows the authority staffed or performing supervisory checks, the June 2026 Reform Agenda test.
The Reform Agenda gives the baseline as no competent authority for NIS2 and sets a June 2026 target. Designation in the June 2025 law is the change that matters.
The new export system is a Reform Agenda step with a June 2027 target. No item reports it implemented.

North Macedonia reported the platform as being developed at the 2023 screening. The evidence is reported only and has not been updated since July 2023, so the status at the freeze date is the last known one.
The last evidence, a February 2025 report of North Macedonia's own statement, says the decision awaited adoption and was expected in January 2025. No later item shows whether it was adopted.
The law sets a 15-month deadline for by-laws, and the Commission repeated this in May 2026 without reporting them adopted. The ICT strategy lists preparing them as an activity.
North Macedonia described the law at the screening as the general labour law containing a non-discrimination rule. No independent item shows how it is applied, so I stop at adopted.

The reform as a whole is a Reform Agenda plan for infrastructure, 5G and related law. A new Law on Electronic Communications was adopted in June 2025 as one part, but no item shows the secure infrastructure rolled out.

The 2025 law establishes the national and governmental teams, with the governmental team to start within 12 months of entry into force, but no item shows either operating to NIS2 and SIM3 standard. The Reform Agenda's baseline says not operational (2024), while the regulator reports MKD-CIRT handling incidents and North Macedonia says it is in place; the baseline may mean NIS2 readiness only.

The Commission twice names the e-Tax system among e-services that simplified tax reporting, and this is independent of the government's description. The evidence shows use, not success, and the latest item is a 2025 reported statement.
The items describe a planned investment and project. A feasibility study had only started by October 2025, and no item shows the network built.
North Macedonia requested access and the Commission took note, saying it is being considered under the Growth Plan. No item shows access granted.
North Macedonia says it is not aligned and plans to align by 2028, and the Commission confirms in November 2025 that it still needs to do so.
The items are only rows of the 2021-2023 plan, each worded as an action to be done, and the plan's period has ended. No item states that the plan was adopted or says what was delivered.

The Agency reports in three of its own documents that it holds observer status in the Board. No independent item confirms its participation, so government reporting alone does not support in practice.
The Commission and the Agency's report both state that the Assembly amended the law to allow transfers to NATO countries without prior consultation. No item shows transfers made under it.

The screening reports state that all by-laws were adopted in the first half of 2020. The Commission disputes whether this achieved eIDAS harmonisation, but that is a question of alignment, not of whether the by-laws were adopted.
North Macedonia cites the law at the screening as part of the framework for companies. There is no independent evidence of application in these items.

The Commission says access to public information improved thanks to the strategy adopted in November 2019, which suggests it was carried out. The evidence is one 2020 passage, and the strategy's period ended in 2021 with no item showing an extension.
The World Bank lists the project as to be agreed and in preparation in September 2024. No later item shows approval.
